builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: RLGPA: A Reinforcement Learning-Guided Granularity Planning Attack for Decision-Based Sparse Adversarial Examples
summary: RLGPA replaces heuristic or fixed-policy strategies for sparse adversarial example generation with an online reinforcement learning scheduler that dynamically selects support-reduction executors and granularity. The method incurs the cost of training a Dueling Double DQN planner and managing state-conditioned action masking, which increases implementation complexity compared to baseline attacks. Success depends on the availability of a decision-based oracle and may fail if the victim model changes its labeling behavior or if the query budget is insufficient for the RL policy to converge.
rationale: This technique is relevant for security researchers and practitioners evaluating model robustness against decision-based adversarial attacks, but it introduces a method for generating attacks rather than defending against them, making it unsuitable for production adoption focused on model deployment.

claims.statement: RLGPA replaces heuristic or fixed-policy strategies for sparse adversarial example generation with an online reinforcement learning scheduler that dynamically selects support-reduction executors and granularity. The method incurs the cost of training a Dueling Double DQN planner and managing state-conditioned action masking, which increases implementation complexity compared to baseline attacks. Success depends on the availability of a decision-based oracle and may fail if the victim model changes its labeling behavior or if the query budget is insufficient for the RL policy to converge.
RLGPA reaches 61% targeted ASR at sparsity 0.01 on CIFAR-10 (vs. 25% SparseEvo, 0% Pointwise), and 75.5%/73.0% on ResNet50/ViT at sparsity 0.005 (vs. 29.0%/15.5%).
